nanoGPT, the small GPT trainer

A map of karpathy/nanoGPT at commit 3adf61e in C4 terms: context on the overview, the scripts and their components on the full map. The README now notes the project is deprecated in favour of nanochat; this map describes the code as it stands.

panels.overviewHtml:
The full map

Scripts that hand off through files

There is no long-running service. Each script runs, reads and writes files, and exits. train.py and model.py are opened into their components.

How to read it

The person on the left, the scripts in the middle, the model library they all import, then the files on disk and the outside services they download from.

people.title: People
people.text: nanoGPT has no users in the service sense: whoever runs the scripts is the only actor.

prep.title: Prepare the data
prep.text: One script per dataset turns raw text into train.bin and val.bin.

train.title: Train
train.text: train.py: a ~300-line script that sets up a run and loops until max_iters.

model.title: The GPT model
model.text: model.py: the whole network plus helpers to load GPT-2 weights and generate text.

use.title: Sample and benchmark
use.text: Two small scripts that use the model outside the training loop.

files.title: Files on disk
files.text: The scripts share no process; they hand work to each other through these files.

outside.title: Outside services
outside.text: Downloaded at prep or init time; W&B only when wandb_log is on.

nodes.what: Runs the scripts from a shell: prepares a dataset, trains or finetunes with a config file and flags, then samples text from the result.
nodes.why: There is no server and no UI. Every run is a command line, and every setting is a Python global the person can override.

nodes.what: Serves the OpenWebText dataset to datasets.load_dataset and OpenAI's released GPT-2 weights to transformers.GPT2LMHeadModel.from_pretrained.
nodes.why: Reproducing GPT-2 needs ~9B tokens of web text and the four GPT-2 checkpoints as baselines and finetuning starts; nanoGPT downloads both rather than shipping them.
nodes.tools: datasets and transformers libraries, cached locally by them (the OWT comment says ~54 GB in the HF cache)

nodes.what: One ~1 MB text file from the char-rnn repository, fetched over HTTPS with requests on first run.
nodes.why: The smallest real dataset that still produces recognisable output, so a first run takes minutes, not days.
nodes.tools: raw.githubusercontent.com/karpathy/char-rnn/.../tinyshakespeare/input.txt, saved as input.txt next to the script

nodes.what: Receives train and val loss, learning rate and MFU at every evaluation when wandb_log=True.
nodes.why: Multi-day runs need curves you can watch from elsewhere. It is off by default and only the master process logs.
nodes.tools: wandb client, imported only when enabled · on in config/train_gpt2.py

nodes.what: Downloads OpenWebText, splits off 0.05% as validation, encodes every document with the GPT-2 BPE in 8 processes, appends an end-of-text token and writes each split as one flat uint16 array.
nodes.why: Training reads random windows straight from disk, so all tokenisation happens once, ahead of time. The ~17 GB train.bin is the price.
nodes.tools: datasets · tiktoken gpt2 encoding · np.memmap · tqdm. Not visible in this repo: tiktoken downloads its GPT-2 BPE files from OpenAI on first use and caches them.

nodes.what: Downloads tiny Shakespeare, takes the first 90% as train and the rest as val, and encodes both with the GPT-2 BPE.
nodes.why: Finetuning a pretrained GPT-2 needs the same 50257-token vocabulary it was trained with, so this dataset uses BPE, not characters.
nodes.tools: requests · tiktoken (fetches its GPT-2 BPE files on first use; not visible in this repo) · numpy.tofile

nodes.what: Downloads tiny Shakespeare, builds a 65-symbol vocabulary from the characters it contains, encodes a 90/10 split, and saves the mapping in meta.pkl.
nodes.why: The quick-start dataset: tiny vocabulary, tiny model, a run of minutes. meta.pkl is how training and sampling learn that this dataset is not GPT-2 BPE.

nodes.what: train.bin and val.bin: each split as one long run of uint16 token ids. The character dataset adds meta.pkl with its vocabulary.
nodes.why: The only interface between data prep and training. Any dataset that produces these files can be trained on with --dataset=name.

nodes.what: One torch.save dict with the weights, the optimizer state, the model shape, the iteration and the best val loss. Each save overwrites the last.
nodes.why: It is how a run resumes (init_from='resume') and how sample.py finds a trained model; the stored shape lets both rebuild the exact architecture.

nodes.what: Executed inside train.py, sample.py and bench.py: runs each config file given on the command line, then applies each --key=value to the script's globals, checking the type matches.
nodes.why: No argparse and no config object: every default is a plain global at the top of the script, and config files are just Python that reassigns them.

nodes.what: Detects a DDP run from RANK, seeds and sets autocast, reads meta.pkl for the vocabulary, then builds the model from scratch, from a checkpoint or from GPT-2 weights. Creates AdamW, then compiles and wraps the model.
nodes.why: One script covers a laptop CPU run and an 8-GPU node: the same code path, with DDP, mixed precision and torch.compile switched by globals.

nodes.what: Picks batch_size random offsets in train.bin or val.bin and returns inputs x and the same windows shifted by one token as targets y, moved to the GPU without blocking.
nodes.why: A "poor man's data loader": no Dataset class, no workers, no epochs. Random windows over one flat array are all a language model needs.
nodes.tools: np.memmap recreated per batch (to avoid a memory leak) · pinned memory · train.py get_batch

nodes.what: Each iteration sets the learning rate, runs gradient_accumulation_steps forward/backward micro-steps, clips gradients, steps AdamW and logs loss and MFU.
nodes.why: This is where a 0.5M-token batch is built out of micro-batches that fit in memory, and where DDP syncs gradients only once per step.
nodes.tools: train.py lines 249-333 · cosine LR with warmup · torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler for float16 · DDP

nodes.what: Under torchrun, N copies of train.py run, one per GPU, possibly across nodes. Each reads RANK, LOCAL_RANK and WORLD_SIZE, joins an NCCL process group, divides gradient_accumulation_steps by the world size, and all-reduces gradients on the last micro-step. Only rank 0 evaluates, logs and checkpoints.
nodes.why: This is how the GPT-2 124M run uses 8 GPUs for one ~0.5M-token batch. Without RANK set, train.py runs as a single process and none of this happens.

nodes.what: Every eval_interval iterations, on the master process only, averages the loss over eval_iters batches of each split, logs it, and writes ckpt.pt if val improved or always_save_checkpoint is on.
nodes.why: The one place a run reports progress and leaves something usable behind. eval_only=True turns a training run into a pure evaluation (the GPT-2 baseline configs).

nodes.what: Token and position embeddings, a stack of n_layer Blocks, a final LayerNorm and a language-model head tied to the token embedding. Returns logits, and the cross-entropy loss when targets are given.
nodes.why: The whole architecture in one ~300-line file, shaped to match GPT-2 so that OpenAI's weights load into it.

nodes.what: Pre-norm residual block: causal self-attention then a 4x-wide GELU MLP, each added back to the input.
nodes.why: Repeated n_layer times; the attention uses PyTorch's fused scaled_dot_product_attention when available and an explicit masked softmax otherwise.

nodes.what: Builds a GPT with the shape of gpt2, -medium, -large or -xl, loads Hugging Face's GPT-2 and copies every tensor across, transposing the four Conv1D weight matrices.
nodes.why: Lets nanoGPT evaluate, finetune and sample from OpenAI's checkpoints without adopting the transformers model code.

nodes.what: Repeats max_new_tokens times: crop the context to block_size, run the model, scale the last logits by temperature, keep the top k, sample one token and append it.
nodes.why: Plain sampling with no KV cache: each new token re-runs the whole context, which keeps the code short at the cost of speed.

nodes.what: Loads a model from out_dir/ckpt.pt or a GPT-2 variant, picks the character codec from meta.pkl or falls back to GPT-2 BPE, encodes the prompt and prints num_samples generations.
nodes.why: The way to see what a run learned. It has to find the right tokenizer on its own, because the checkpoint stores the dataset name but not the vocabulary.
nodes.tools: sample.py · tiktoken (downloads the GPT-2 BPE files on first use, outside this repo's code) · prompt from --start or FILE:

nodes.what: A cut-down training loop on a fixed 124M-shaped model with real OpenWebText batches or random tokens; reports time per iteration and MFU, or records a PyTorch profiler trace.
nodes.why: Measures speed without the rest of train.py: no gradient accumulation, no evaluation, no checkpoints.

prepare.title: Prepare a dataset
prepare.desc: The quick start: tiny Shakespeare becomes character ids in two flat files plus a vocabulary pickle.

hops.t: python data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py. No arguments: paths are relative to the script's own folder.
If input.txt is not there yet, it is downloaded once from the char-rnn repository and saved beside the script.
About 1.1 million characters. Every distinct character becomes a token: 65 of them, sorted, so ids are stable between runs.
The first 90% is encoded to train.bin, the last 10% to val.bin, both as uint16. meta.pkl stores vocab_size, stoi and itos.
hops.note: The BPE datasets (openwebtext, shakespeare) write the same two .bin files but no meta.pkl; that absence is what tells later scripts to use GPT-2 BPE.

start.title: Start a training run from scratch
start.desc: The quick start, python train.py config/train_shakespeare_char.py: config overrides, the vocabulary from meta.pkl, a freshly initialised GPT, then the loop.

hops.t: python train.py config/train_shakespeare_char.py. Any --key=value after it wins over the file, e.g. --device=cpu --compile=False on a laptop.

configurator.py is exec'd into train.py's globals: the config sets dataset='shakespeare_char', a 6-layer, 6-head, 384-wide model with a 256-token context, batch 64, dropout 0.2, 5000 iterations and out_dir='out-shakespeare-char'. init_from keeps its default, 'scratch'.
train.py finds data/shakespeare_char/meta.pkl and reads vocab_size = 65. Without a meta.pkl (the BPE datasets) a from-scratch model gets 50304, GPT-2's 50257 rounded up for efficiency.
GPT(GPTConfig(**model_args)): weights drawn from N(0, 0.02), the residual projections scaled down by the depth, token embedding tied to the output head.
hops.note: The other two branches: init_from='resume' loads out_dir/ckpt.pt and restores weights, optimizer state, iter_num and best_val_loss; init_from='gpt2*' calls GPT.from_pretrained (as config/finetune_shakespeare.py does with gpt2-xl).

hops.t: AdamW is created with weight decay only on 2-D tensors, the model is compiled (unless --compile=False), and wrapped in DDP if RANK is set. The loop starts at iteration 0 (or at the saved iteration on resume).

step.title: One training iteration
step.desc: Learning rate, several forward/backward micro-steps over random windows, one optimizer step.

hops.t: The first batch was fetched before the loop began. Each micro-step uses the current X, Y.
get_batch opens train.bin as a fresh np.memmap, draws batch_size random start offsets and slices block_size tokens from each; targets are the same slices one token later.
Under autocast (bfloat16 or float16 on GPU), model(X, Y) returns logits and the cross-entropy loss, which is divided by the number of accumulation steps.
Inside, token and position embeddings pass through n_layer blocks of causal attention and MLP before the tied output head.
While the GPU still works on that forward pass, the next batch is fetched and copied over asynchronously (pinned memory, non-blocking).
scaler.scale(loss).backward() accumulates gradients over the micro-steps.
Under DDP only: on the last micro-step the backward pass also all-reduces gradients with the other ranks over NCCL, so every rank holds the same averaged gradient.
hops.note: After all micro-steps: unscale, clip the gradient norm to 1.0, step AdamW and the GradScaler, zero the gradients.

eval.title: Evaluate and save a checkpoint
eval.desc: Every eval_interval iterations, on the master process: estimate both losses, log them and maybe overwrite ckpt.pt.

hops.t: At the top of the iteration, when iter_num % eval_interval == 0 and this is rank 0 (or the only process).
estimate_loss switches the model to eval mode and draws eval_iters random batches from train.bin and from val.bin.
Forward passes under torch.no_grad(); the mean loss per split is the estimate. Then the model goes back to train mode.
If wandb_log is on: iteration, both losses, learning rate and MFU.

If val loss beat the best so far, or always_save_checkpoint is on, and this is not iteration 0: weights, optimizer state, model_args, iter_num, best_val_loss and the full config go into out_dir/ckpt.pt, replacing the previous file.
hops.note: With always_save_checkpoint on, best_val_loss is overwritten with the current val loss even when it got worse.

sample.title: Sample text from a trained model
sample.desc: python sample.py --out_dir=out-shakespeare-char: rebuild the model from the checkpoint, find its tokenizer, generate.

hops.t: python sample.py --out_dir=out-shakespeare-char, optionally with --start="..." or --start=FILE:prompt.txt.
The same configurator overrides sample.py's globals: init_from='resume', 10 samples of 500 tokens, temperature 0.8, top-k 200 by default.
ckpt.pt is loaded; model_args rebuilds the exact GPT and the weights are loaded after stripping any _orig_mod. prefix.
The checkpoint's config names the dataset; if data/<dataset>/meta.pkl exists, its stoi/itos become the codec. Otherwise tiktoken's GPT-2 BPE is used.
The prompt is encoded to a 1 x T tensor and model.generate is called once per sample.
Each new token: crop the context to block_size, forward it (only the last position goes through the output head), divide by temperature, keep the top k, softmax, draw one token, append.
The finished sequence is decoded back to text and printed, followed by a separator line.

buildSteps.title: Tokens on disk
buildSteps.text: Turn a small text into integer ids in two flat files.
buildSteps.decision: Each split is one uint16 array with no index or document boundaries, so the loader can memory-map it and read any window.

buildSteps.title: A GPT
buildSteps.text: Embeddings, a stack of transformer blocks and a tied output head.
buildSteps.decision: Parameter names and shapes follow GPT-2 exactly, which is what later makes OpenAI's weights loadable.

buildSteps.title: A training loop
buildSteps.text: Configure with globals, build the model, fetch random windows, step AdamW.
buildSteps.decision: Configuration is plain Python globals overridden by exec'd files and flags, so every hyperparameter is visible at the top of the script.

buildSteps.title: Evaluation and checkpoints
buildSteps.text: Estimate train and val loss now and then and save the model.
buildSteps.decision: The checkpoint stores the model shape and the config with the weights, so other scripts can rebuild it without knowing the run.

buildSteps.title: Sampling
buildSteps.text: Load a checkpoint and generate text token by token.
buildSteps.decision: The tokenizer is not in the checkpoint: sample.py finds meta.pkl through the dataset name, or assumes GPT-2 BPE.

buildSteps.title: Scale to GPT-2
buildSteps.text: OpenWebText, GPT-2 weights for finetuning and baselines, multi-GPU training, logging and benchmarks.
buildSteps.decision: Nothing in the loop changes: DDP, a larger dataset and pretrained weights are switched on by globals in config files.

tour.title: A GPT trainer in a few files
body: nanoGPT trains and finetunes GPT-2-style language models. It is a set of scripts, not a service: one person runs them in order from a shell.
Data prep scripts download text and tokenize it, train.py trains a model defined in model.py, and sample.py generates text from the result. Hugging Face supplies datasets and GPT-2 weights.
tour.why: Each script is short enough to read in one sitting; the files on disk are the only thing they share.

tour.title: Text becomes token files
body: Follow the quick-start dataset from a download to train.bin, val.bin and meta.pkl.
tour.why: Tokenising ahead of time makes the training loader trivial: random slices of one array.

tour.title: Setting up a run
body: A config file and flags set globals, then the model is built: here from scratch, sized by the dataset's vocabulary.
tour.why: The same setup code handles training from scratch, resuming and finetuning; init_from picks the branch.

tour.title: One iteration of the loop
body: Random windows in, loss out, gradients accumulated over micro-steps, one optimizer step.
tour.why: Gradient accumulation and DDP are how a ~0.5M-token batch fits on 8 GPUs of 40 GB.

tour.title: Measure and save
body: Every few hundred or thousand iterations the master process estimates both losses and may write ckpt.pt.
tour.why: The checkpoint carries enough to rebuild the model, which is what sampling and resuming rely on.

tour.title: Generate text
body: sample.py rebuilds the model from the checkpoint, finds its tokenizer and samples token by token.
tour.why: No KV cache: every token re-runs the cropped context, simple at the cost of speed.

tour.title: The whole of nanoGPT, on one map

recap.people: One person runs the scripts with configs and flags.
recap.prep: Prepare scripts tokenize text once into flat files.
recap.files: Token files and one checkpoint connect the scripts.
recap.train: train.py sets up the run and loops: batches, forward, backward, step.
recap.model: model.py holds the GPT, GPT-2 weight import and sampling.
recap.use: sample.py generates text; bench.py times the hot loop.
recap.outside: Hugging Face and GitHub supply data and weights; W&B logs runs.

body: Scripts that hand off through files: prepare, train, sample.
The design choice that shapes everything: plain, readable code over abstractions, with every setting a global you can override.

loop.title: Inside the training loop
loop.sub: One pass of the while True loop in train.py, in order.
loop.cap: Logging reads loss.item(), which forces the CPU to wait for the GPU; that is why it only happens every log_interval iterations and on the master process.

steps.d: Linear warmup, then cosine decay to min_lr; constant if decay_lr is off.
Every eval_interval iterations on the master process.

steps.t: Gradient sync only on the last micro-step
steps.d: Under DDP, toggles require_backward_grad_sync instead of using no_sync().
While the GPU runs the forward pass.
Scaling is a no-op unless the dtype is float16.

steps.t: Step AdamW, update the scaler, free the gradients

steps.d: MFU is a running average, started after 5 iterations.

exit.t: Leave the loop, tear down DDP

gpt.title: Inside the GPT forward pass
gpt.sub: What GPT.forward(idx, targets) does with a batch of token ids.
gpt.cap: The token embedding and the output head are the same matrix (weight tying), so the 50304 x n_embd table is stored and trained once.

steps.d: Flash attention via scaled_dot_product_attention when PyTorch has it; otherwise a masked softmax over a stored lower-triangular mask.
Linear to 4x width, GELU, linear back, dropout.
With targets, the head runs on every position.

exit.t: Head on the last position only, no loss

tokens.title: Inside the token files
tokens.sub: What each prepare script leaves in data/<dataset>/, and what train.py and sample.py read back.
tokens.cap: There is no index and no document boundary in the .bin files: OpenWebText separates documents only by an end-of-text token (50256), and the loader samples windows that may span two documents.

tables.name: train.bin
tables.note: The training split as one long array.

fields.note: GPT-2 BPE id (below 50257) or a character id (below 65); fits because the largest id is under 2^16
file size / 2; ~9B tokens (~17 GB) for OpenWebText, ~1M for character Shakespeare
Shakespeare: the last 10% of the text; OpenWebText: a random 0.05% of documents
65; train.py sizes the model from it
character to id, used by sample.py to encode
id to character, used to decode

ckpt.title: Inside ckpt.pt
ckpt.cap: One file per out_dir, overwritten on each save. State-dict keys can carry an _orig_mod. prefix (probably from saving a torch.compiled model); both loaders strip it.

tables.name: checkpoint
tables.note: Everything needed to resume or sample.

fields.note: AdamW moments; only resume reads it
every global of the run; sample.py reads config['dataset'] to find meta.pkl

tables.name: model_args
tables.note: The model's shape, so GPTConfig can be rebuilt.

fields.note: 50304 by default from scratch, 50257 from GPT-2, 65 for characters
the only one resume lets the command line change
